stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg makes deal with Meta to help him pay California billionaire tax, if it passes
stories.summary: The Meta boss said he would exit the state over a wealth tax that has not yet come into force. Meta has agreed a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to stop the Facebook co-founder from leaving California after he threatened to move from the state because of a proposed tax on billionaires. The agreement allows Zuckerberg - reportedly one of the world's richest people - to sell shares in Meta without losing control of the Californian-based company if he needs to pay a large tax bill. The measure, which would impose a one-time 5% tax on state residents with a net worth of more than $1bn (£750m), is yet to pass. Californian residents will vote on 3 November.

stories.title: A final farewell to NYC’s horse carriage industry
stories.summary: GOODBYE HORSES: New York City isn’t horsing around anymore. The City Council voted overwhelmingly today to abolish the Big Apple’s horse carriage industry, handing a historic win to animal rights activists who’ve pushed to end the tourist attraction for decades. The vote doesn’t mean the industry sunsets overnight, though. The bill enacting the ban — which passed the Council with 40 yays, 7 nays and 2 abstentions — allows the roughly 200 carriage drivers who shuttle tourists around Central Park to continue operating until June 2028, when the industry will be reined into a legal halt officially. stories.title: US judge orders Trump administration to halt noncitizen voting investigation
stories.summary: Federal judge says government’s investigation into alleged noncitizen voting in nine states is relying on flawed data A federal judge in California has ordered the Trump administration to halt investigations in nine states into whether noncitizens are registered to vote. US district court judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in Oakland found the government’s effort was relying on data that is full of errors and that it was leading to intimidation of groups performing voter assistance efforts. She said it should be halted until polls close on election day on 3 November.

stories.title: Fantasy Football Managers Should Sell High on Tre Tucker After a Misleading Breakout
stories.summary: Tre Tucker performed excellently in Week 6 with two touchdowns, but his competition, red-zone usage, target share, among other metrics, make him a sell-high candidate. Tucker is averaging 5.8 targets, 4.0 receptions, 61.8 yards, and 0.5 touchdowns per game. He has a 74% snap rate on passing plays. Overall, Tucker's target share comes to 17%, tied for second-best on the team. The Raiders have spread the ball around. Four pass-catchers average more than five targets per game, and each accounts for more than 16% of the team's targets. Those names are Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, Tucker, and Michael Mayer.
